wine.name: Merengő Egri Bikavér Superior
wine.classification: Superior, the middle of the three tiers of Egri Bikavér
wine.grapes: Kékfrankos at the core, with Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Pinot Noir and Syrah in the vintage the house details; the mix moves with the year.
wine.sites: Several of the estate's vineyards in the Eger district, blended to a house style rather than for one site; parcels on the Nagy-Eged hill, a limestone outcrop above Eger, help shape the blend.
wine.making: Fermented for about three weeks in stainless steel or open vats, as the house describes it. The wine then ages for about fifteen months in 500 litre barrels of Hungarian oak, and rests in bottle before release, as the rules for the blend require.
wine.glass: Black cherry, ripe plum and blackcurrant with a peppery edge from Kékfrankos and a touch of cocoa from the barrel; deeper and firmer than a classic Bikavér, with ripe tannin and fresh acidity.
wine.ageing: Approachable on release after its time in barrel and bottle, it gains savoury depth over the next five to ten years in a cool cellar.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Bordeaux glass.

records.table: Merengő is St. Andrea's Egri Bikavér Superior, a Kékfrankos led blend from the Egerszalók estate, aged about fifteen months in large Hungarian oak. Deeper and firmer than a classic Bikavér, it carries black cherry and pepper; give it an hour in a decanter.
records.story: Bikavér means bull's blood, and the story goes that the name was born in the siege of Eger in 1552, when the castle's defenders drank red wine and the besieging Turks took it for blood. It is told as a legend: Hungary then made mostly white wine, and the earliest known document naming an Eger Bikavér dates from 1851. St. Andrea came much later. A family founded the estate in 2002 at Egerszalók, a village east of Eger in the foothills of the Bükk, and named it, by the house's account, in honour of the founder's wife; the family's first wine, a Cabernet Sauvignon of 1997, came before the estate. From the start the house built its range around Bikavér. Its first single vineyard Bikavér came from the Hangács vineyard at Demjén with the 2007 vintage, and Merengő took its place as the house's Superior, the blend made to a style across several sites rather than from one. In 2023 the district's rules were rewritten and Egri Bikavér gained a protected designation of its own. For a sommelier, Merengő shows what the middle tier of the blend can be: Kékfrankos at the centre, more depth and grip than a classic Bikavér, yet fresh and peppery.

wine.name: Egri Bikavér Grand Superior Nagy-Eged dűlő
wine.classification: Grand Superior, the highest of the three tiers of Egri Bikavér, from one named vineyard
wine.grapes: Kékfrankos, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Syrah and Kadarka, planted together in the proportions of the intended blend.
wine.sites: The Nagy-Eged dűlő on the southern slopes of the Nagy-Eged hill above Eger, a limestone outcrop rising to about 500 metres, unlike the volcanic tuff of most of the district; planted in 2008.
wine.making: The five varieties, planted together in 2008 in the proportions of the finished wine, are picked together and fermented together, rather than made apart and blended later. wine.glass: Black cherry, cassis and red plum with violet and a peppery lift from Kékfrankos, cedar and a little cocoa from the barrel; firm, fine tannin and the bright, racy acidity of the limestone hill.
wine.ageing: Tight in its first years, it opens some five years after the vintage and should hold its freshness for a decade and more.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or two; a Bordeaux glass.

records.table: Thummerer's Egri Bikavér Grand Superior comes from vines planted together on the Nagy-Eged hill in 2008, picked and fermented together as a field blend, then given eighteen months in barrel. Cherry, cassis and pepper ride on bright limestone acidity; decant it.
records.story: Vilmos Thummerer (1943 to 2021) and his wife bought their first vineyards in the Eger district in 1984, while Hungary was a communist state, and began making wine at Noszvaj, a village east of Eger in the Bükk foothills. The estate cellar there had been cut into volcanic tuff by hand more than a century before, and in 2004 a second cellar system was dug beside it. In 1995 he was named Hungary's Winemaker of the Year, and the house became a familiar name for Bikavér and Kékfrankos. In 2008 the family planted a block on the southern slopes of the Nagy-Eged, the limestone hill above Eger, with the five varieties of its intended blend in the proportions of the finished wine, so that the vineyard itself would make the cuvée: the grapes are picked together and fermented together. That wine became the house's Grand Superior, named for its dűlő. Vilmos Thummerer died in December 2021. For a sommelier the Grand Superior is a lesson in Bikavér as a field blend: one hill planted to a plan, rather than a cellar assembly of separate wines.

records.story: Tibor Gál (1958 to 2005) was an Eger winemaker when, in 1989, after a visit and a tasting, he was invited to Tuscany by the founder of Tenuta dell'Ornellaia in Bolgheri. There he rose from cellar hand to chief winemaker, and the young estate made its name in his years. By the house's own account the family came home to Hungary at the end of 1992 and he founded the winery at Eger; other accounts date its start to 1993. One of his aims was to bring Egri Bikavér back to the standing it had lost, and he went on advising estates abroad as well. On 10 February 2005, returning from work at a winery in South Africa, he died in a road accident, aged 46. His son, who shares his name, took on the house and turned its Bikavér towards single vineyards: Síkhegy, on rhyolite tuff, and Pajados, the lighter of the two, both labelled Grand Superior, the uppermost tier of the blend. The winery carries the founder's name in the Hungarian order, family name first. For a sommelier, Pajados links Bolgheri and Eger, and shows the fresher, Kadarka scented side of Bull's Blood.

wine.name: Egri Bikavér
wine.grapes: Kékfrankos at the core, with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and other red grapes of the district such as Zweigelt and Blauburger; the mix moves with the year.
wine.sites: The house's vineyards in the Eger district, blended from several sites rather than one; the winery itself stands in an old stone quarry on the edge of the town.
wine.making: Fermented in stainless steel with the grapes' own yeasts, then aged in Hungarian oak barrels, a part of them new and small, for well over a year before blending and bottling.
wine.glass: Black cherry and stewed plum with a smoky, inky note and a hint of chocolate; medium in body, with fresh acidity and dry, grainy tannin.
wine.ageing: Ready on release, it drinks well for four to six years and is made to be poured young rather than laid down.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a medium sized red wine glass.

records.table: Bolyki's Egri Bikavér is the everyday face of Eger's Bull's Blood: Kékfrankos led, aged over a year in Hungarian oak, made in a winery built into an old quarry outside the town. Black cherry, smoke and fresh acidity make it a red for the table rather than the cellar.
records.story: Phylloxera reached Eger in 1886 and almost wiped out its vineyards, and the Bikavér blend of the twentieth century took shape in the replanting that followed, at the start of the twentieth century. Bolyki opens a newer chapter. It began in 1998 with a first generation winemaker whose parents had grown grapes in their garden for a little extra income. The house made its home in a disused stone quarry on the edge of Eger: walls some 30 metres high enclose the winery, and four pits joined by tunnels serve as its cellars. Around them the family built a range of Bikavér in each tier, a classic Egri Bikavér, a Superior and a Grand Superior from the Öreghegy at Verpelét, beside a varietal Kékfrankos that made the house known in the district. In 2023 the district rewrote its rules, and Egri Bikavér gained a protected designation of its own, a blend of at least four red grapes on a backbone of Kékfrankos. Bolyki's Egri Bikavér is the wine to teach the first step of the ladder: fresh, Kékfrankos led and released to drink, a Bull's Blood for the table rather than the cellar.

records.table: Gróf Buttler's Nagy-Eged Egri Bikavér Superior comes from the house's vines on the limestone Nagy-Eged hill above Eger, planted from 2003. Merlot and Cabernet led in the year the house details, it is round and firm, with fresh acidity; decant it for an hour.
records.story: Eger's red wine story is younger than its white: by the district's own telling, red grapes such as Kadarka, and the way of fermenting on the skins, came with Serbs fleeing the Ottoman advance. Bikavér rules were drafted in 1993 but could only stand as advice; the Egri Bikavér regulations were adopted in 1997 and became official in 2002, setting the tiers that a Superior label names. Gróf Buttler, Count Buttler in Hungarian, was founded at Eger in 1999, with its cellar in the old cellar row of Nagykőporos. It planted first on the volcanic soil of the Szarkás hill in 2000, and in 2003 it moved onto the Nagy-Eged, a limestone outcrop above the town rising to about 500 metres, quite unlike the tuff of most of the district. The house farms only its own vines and makes its reds the traditional way, in open vats and then in oak. Its Superior from the hill bears the hill's name. In 2023 the rules were rewritten and Egri Bikavér gained a protected designation of its own. For a sommelier, this wine shows Bikavér from limestone rather than tuff, and how far the blend's makeup could range from house to house.

report: Founded 1999 by the house's own page and a blog of 2012; Szarkás in 2000 and Nagy-Eged in 2003 rest on the house's page alone, as its own vineyards.

The count the house is named for could not be identified from two sources (a Count János Buttler of Mikszáth's novel A Strange Marriage is a candidate, his dates unconfirmed), so the story names no count.

The house's sheet for its 2018 Nagy-Eged Bikavér Superior lists no Kékfrankos at all (Merlot about half, Cabernet Sauvignon about a quarter, then Syrah, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc, Kadarka); the region record and the advanced quiz say Kékfrankos is compulsory, which holds for the rules of 2023 and may not have held for earlier vintages. The checker should weigh this.

A trade report says the house emerged from bankruptcy with a new team, which a former owner disputes; left out, and the pick may want a check that the house still makes this wine. Barrel length for this wine was not found, so the record gives the tier's minimum of a year, from Decanter and a second guide.
